title: ACP: The Universal Remote Control for AI Agents — Alex Hancock, Block
talk_summary: Alex Hancock (Block, Goose/MCP maintainer) presents ACP (Agent Client Protocol), a JSON-RPC standard letting any client software drive any agent harness, with local stdio and new remote HTTP/websocket transports. The core argument is that standardizing the client-to-harness interface (as MCP did for harness-to-tools) lets the four agentic-stack components — client, harness, tools, model — be relocated independently.

takeaways.technique: Decouple client from harness via a standard protocol
takeaways.what_they_do: ACP defines a JSON-RPC interface so one client implementation can drive any harness (Goose, Poolside, etc.), and one harness can be driven by any client, with sessions, streaming updates, tool-call notifications, and permission requests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one implementation on the harness side, and you can now use any client

takeaways.technique: Remote transport for the agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They added an HTTP transport plus websocket upgrade to ACP so the harness can run in a container or cloud while the client stays local, with identical message semantics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the messages are the same, the protocol semantics are the same, but there's a new transport that is just landing now that enables remote

takeaways.technique: Extensible protocol with underscore-prefixed custom methods
takeaways.what_they_do: ACP allows vendor-specific methods (prefixed with underscore) so implementations can experiment, and common patterns can later be promoted into the standard.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you put an underscore, and then you start to put your custom methods
